text: 23-year-old college student. The patient is here for a follow-up appointment. He was recently diagnosed with schizophrenia and started on risperidone approximately 2 months ago. Reports a significant improvement in psychiatric symptoms since the start of treatment.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information. Since you started risperidone two months ago, have you noticed any involuntary muscle stiffness, slowness of movement, or a resting tremor in your hands?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Inability to remain still, persistent feeling of restlessness. I also have Frequent fidgeting, Repetitive crossing and uncrossing of legs, Pacing.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The symptoms you describe, such as restlessness and pacing, are classic signs of akathisia, a common side effect of risperidone. To confirm this and rule out other causes, I need to know if you have any family history of movement disorders or if you have used any other psychiatric medications in the past.

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal AIMS scale rules out tardive dyskinesia, which strongly supports my suspicion of akathisia given your restlessness and risperidone use. Do you experience any muscle rigidity or a slow, shuffling gait that would suggest parkinsonism instead?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Recently diagnosed with schizophrenia. No other significant past medical history. Social history: College student, lives with parents. Denies tobacco, alcohol, or drug use.

speaker: Doctor
text: Good, the absence of substance use helps rule out other causes for your restlessness. Do you find that these feelings of inner tension and the urge to move are significantly worse when you try to sit still or lie down?
